abstract: This article examines using a parallel plate capacitor sensor for accurately measuring void fraction in dielectric fluids. Unlike traditional concave and rod methods, the parallel plate configuration provides a significant advantage by ensuring a linear electric field distribution throughout the measurable volume. With a circular cross-section, the sensor uses metal plates insulated from the fluid by a high dielectric constant material. The choice of insulator is critical, as its high dielectric constant significantly enhances sensitivity, allowing for more pronounced variations in relative capacitance, considering both the sensing area and stray capacitances. Consequently, the total capacitance effectively captures subtle changes in void fraction, making the parallel plate capacitor sensor an excellent choice for applications requiring precise fluid characterization.

articleTitle: URUCON 2024 Abstract Page
Awareness workshops to promote innovation in the public sector
abstract: The Government of Montevideo implemented awareness workshops to promote innovation in collaboration with the Postgraduate Program in Technology and Innovation Management of the University of the Republic. After the initial diagnosis, a group of civil servants was trained to give innovation awareness workshops to other people who also work in the institution. Agile methodologies, problem-based learning, exponential scaled methodology and people-centered public innovation were applied. The experience, which involved more than $\mathbf{1, 5 0 0}$ employees, left the institution with specific practical material and empowered people who strengthen the culture of innovation. There is also a section on lessons learned and recommendations for future initiatives.

articleTitle: URUCON 2024 Abstract Page
Ramp-Response Time-Domain Dielectric Spectroscopy: Proof of concept numerical analysis
abstract: Dielectric Spectroscopy (DS) probes the interaction of matter with time-varying electric fields on frequencies ranging from mHz up to THz. In the lumpedelements approach, the high-frequency limit can reach the hundreds of MHz. DS has gained great interest in biomedical applications. Current methodologies for assessing the complex dielectric permittivity offer advantages and drawbacks. In this context, developing a new measurement approach may offer distinct advantages not found in existing techniques. We present a novel time-domain method, which entails placing the material of interest in a capacitor sample cell connected to a pair of Operational Transconductance Amplifiers (OTA) serving as a gyrator to invert its impedance. The system’s voltage response to a current ramp renders a step-response of the dielectric permittivity (i.e., in the time domain). Fitting the response voltage to dielectric models (e.g., Debye, Cole-Cole) provides the full spectrum model of the complex permittivity. The significance of this development lies in the directness of its results obtained rapidly while being cost-effective. It must be noted that the high-frequency limit of the system is constrained by the component specifications, primarily the OTA.

articleTitle: Exploring Diverse Machine Learning Approaches for Coronary CT Images Analysis: A Comparative Study
abstract: This study evaluates the performance of various machine learning algorithms on coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA) images for detecting coronary atherosclerosis. The algorithms include Logistic Regression (LR), Naïve Bayes (NB), K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN), Decision Trees (DT), Random Forest (RF), Support Vector Machines (SVM), Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP), Recurrent Neural Network (RNN), Convolutional Neural Network (CNN), and Convolutional Neural Network with Transfer Learning (CNN w/ TL). Performance metrics such as Accuracy, Recall, F1-Score, and Area Under the Curve (AUC) are used to compare their effectiveness on separate validation and test datasets. The results highlight $\mathrm{CNN} \mathbf{w / T L}$ as the most effective algorithm, achieving an AUC of $\mathbf{0. 9 1}$ on the validation dataset. The CNN models also perform well, with all metrics over 0.80. Random Forest (RF) demonstrates robust performance with metrics at 0.75 (Validation) and 0.70 (Test).

articleTitle: A Hardware Virtualization Scheme for Reconfigurable Service Providing in the Internet of Things Era
abstract: With the emergence of the Internet of Things, there is a growing demand for distributed and federated processing in consortium with several devices. One current trend is to use devices as processing hubs, providing services such as Software as a Service, Hardware as a Service and Storage as a Service. In this context, reconfigurable computing with Field-Programmable Gate Arrays (FPGAs) brings a new perspective since modern devices have hardware/software flexibility to change their behaviour according to the application. A Hardware as a Service (HaS) scheme for hardware virtualization is necessary to support the different demands. Integrating software applications with FPGA implementations via their physical interfaces (IO) poses considerable challenges, hindering the integration of software and hardware solutions. This paper introduces a software architecture paired with FPGA technology to establish an isolated, decoupled, and scalable testing environment. The proposed methodology and its implementation demonstrate the efficacy of this approach in facilitating rapid prototyping and deployment. The results indicate successful integration with minimal development effort.

articleTitle: Monitoring the Misti Volcano in Arequipa, Peru Using Space Geodesy Techniques
abstract: This study reviews the monitoring of the Misti volcano in Arequipa, Peru, using space geodesy techniques, particularly GNSS, to detect surface deformations. By employing GNSS receivers and the GAMIT/GLOBK software suite, the research aims for millimeter-level accuracy in measuring surface movements. Data collected from March 11th to May 31st, 2022, was processed to identify deformations, accounting for local tectonic influences. Although no significant volcanic deformation was detected during the study period, the established methodologies and infrastructure provide a robust framework for ongoing and future monitoring efforts.

articleTitle: Graph Neural Network Method for Integrating Spatial-Temporal Data in Electricity Demand Forecasting
abstract: Forecasting electrical energy demand with machine learning models using only temporal information fails to capture the dynamics and interrelationships between different types of electrical grid customers. This research proposes incorporating spatial information through graph neural networks constructed from a GIS. These graphs are based on customer locations, selecting an objective node and nearby neighbors within a specified radius, with edges weighted by direct connections and inverse geographical distance. Experiments forecast demand at 1, 3, 6, 12, and 24-hour horizons for residential, commercial, and official customers, using graphs with radius values of $\mathbf{2 5 0} \mathrm{m}, 500 \mathrm{~m}$, and 750 m. The MPNNLSTM and GCLSTM models outperform the baseline CNNLSTM model, with MPNNLSTM performing well at 6,12, and 24 -hour horizons, and GCLSTM at 1 and 3-hour horizons. Using the radius to define the graph demonstrates improved forecasting accuracy by including spatial information.

articleTitle: Fault Localization in Transmission Lines: Discrete Wavelet Transform vs DS Filter
abstract: This study delves into two fault localization techniques in power transmission systems, specifically focusing on the Discrete Wavelet Transform (DWT) and the DifferentiatorSmoother (DS) filter. The investigation encompasses various transmission line configurations, including transposed, non-transposed, and ideally transposed lines, considering both J. Marti and Bergeron line models. For this purpose, simulations were conducted using the Alternative Transients Program and the Matlab program. The effectiveness of each technique is evaluated by comparing the accuracy of fault distance calculations. Results indicate that while the DS filter generally performs better near terminal ends, the DWT may offer advantages for fault localization in certain scenarios, particularly for nontransposed lines. These findings underscore the importance of considering multiple factors when selecting fault localization methods, contributing to advancements in power system reliability and maintenance practices.

articleTitle: Parametric Analysis Applied to Electrical Studies Using Electromagnetic Transients Programs
abstract: This article aims to introduce the reader to the relevance of parametric analysis in electrical studies using Electromagnetic Transients Program (EMTP) by bringing together some published studies using the Parametric Modeling Suite (PAMSUITE) module of the EMTP-RV software and present an example of a case prepared using a set of other computational tools, including the ATP package. When comparing the traditional approach with parametric analysis, note that the results produced by parametric analysis are much more detailed, with which it is possible to make better informed and more economically viable decisions about the system, such as mitigating losses, failures, and equipment protection, for example.

articleTitle: Attitude Stabilization and Altitude Control of a Twin-Engine Tiltrotor Aerial with Inhomogeneous Propulsion Using Optimal Control
abstract: The present work introduces a nonlinear dynamic model of a twin-engine Tiltrotor aerial platform and designs a controller for attitude and altitude with pole placement as performance criterion. The model is linearized, and subsequently, a control design is performed to obtain the optimal proportional-integral controller using liner matrix inequalities conditions. Additionally, simulations verifies the effectiveness of the design method.

articleTitle: Day-Ahead Photovoltaic Power Forecasting with Limited Data
abstract: Forecasting algorithms for photovoltaic (PV) power generation play an important role in energy management systems. Nevertheless, the precision of machine learning models is significantly compromised when historical data is limited. This situation is challenging for new plants for which a long history of measurements is not yet available. The unpredictable nature of the weather gives the perception that a competitive forecast requires a substantial amount of data and a very complicated algorithm. However, in this manuscript, it was found that using five historical days for the inverse quantification of uncertainty, can implicitly describe complex non-linear relationships between last five-day records and day-ahead PV power generation. The proposed approach learns the emerging patterns across various seasons throughout the year without relying on exogenous data such as air temperature, wind speed, pressure, cloud cover, and relative humidity. Results using real-world data collected at the microgrid of the University of Campinas (UNICAMP) confirm that our proposed model outperforms previous state-of-the-art deep learning models as Long short-term memory (LSTM), Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU) and traditional Autoregressive Integrated Moving Average (ARIMA) statistical model, using limited data. The proposed approach is flexible and can be easily adapted to other PV power generation systems with limited data. The source code is available at https://github.com/byronacunia/Day-Ahead-Photovoltaic-Power-Forecasting-with-Limited-Data.git

articleTitle: Estudio de las corrientes de cortocircuito por cables de guardia OPGW en líneas de Alta Tensión
abstract: Los cables de guardia OPGW, además de proteger la línea frente a descargas atmosféricas, posee en su interior fibra óptica utilizada para comunicaciones. Este tipo de cables suele tener una resistencia eléctrica menor a los cables de guardia convencionales, sometiéndolo a corrientes de falta elevadas. Este estudio se basa en analizar la capacidad de circulación de corriente de cortocircuito por un cable de guardia OPGW cuando se lo conecta en paralelo con un cable de guardia convencional de acero, aplicado a una línea de 150 kV del sistema eléctrico uruguayo.

articleTitle: Estimation of Tidal Energy Potential and Identification of Hotspots Using Random Forest
abstract: Tide tables are used to forecast high and low tide heights. This phenomenon is highly predictable, and current velocities are proportional to tide heights. Therefore, this work aims to correlate current velocity and direction data with tide height at a given moment and apply these data to a Random Forest machine learning model to predict current velocities up to 6 days in advance.

articleTitle: Comparison of extracted I-V curve parameters of a PV solar cell under indoor and outdoor conditions
abstract: We extracted and compared the current-voltage (I-V) parameters of a photovoltaic (PV) solar cell using the single-diode model under both indoor and outdoor conditions. For indoor measurements, a solar simulator with temperature control was implemented. The I-V measurements were performed indoors and outdoors at different irradiance levels, maintaining the cell temperature near $25^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$. We employed two methods for extracting series resistance: one near the opencircuit voltage and another in the linear region of the I-V curve at higher voltages. Results reveal notable differences in the single-diode parameters extracted indoors and outdoors, influenced by factors beyond irradiance and temperature, such as spectral distribution and diffuse irradiance. These findings underscore the need to account for environmental conditions when correlating indoor and outdoor measurements, particularly in the analysis of series and shunt resistances.

articleTitle: Special Session “Untrustworthy AI, Mitigating the Threat of Disinformation with Blockchain”
abstract: One of the major risks associated with the explosion of AI capabilities is the generation and propagation of disinformation. Inaccurate and malicious data threatens multiple dimensions of individual and community well-being including public health, democratic governance, climate change, and national security. The risks have been exacerbated by the cognitive drain due to millisecond device interactions and AI-enhanced social media algorithms. The talk will speak to the nature of the threat and potential means for mitigating identified risks. In particular, techniques and lessons from blockchain technologies can be used to enhance the quality of data used by Large Language Models. In addition, such capabilities can be applied to implementing governance rules and processes to contain the risks associated with disinformation.

articleTitle: Assessing the Economic Impact on the Isolated Microgrid System of Brus Laguna during the Solar Eclipses of October 2023 and April 2024
abstract: Abstrac In our era, the electrification of isolated communities and the widespread use of renewable energy sources such as solar and wind are considered increasingly fundamental priorities to counteract the effects of climate change. While solar energy is an economical and easily implementable alternative, it is also highly susceptible to weather conditions such as clouds, rain, or eclipses. Although eclipses do not occur frequently, they significantly impact solar photovoltaic energy generation. In isolated communities with hybrid microgrids that include solar and thermal generation components, this impact is felt more intensely. This paper analyzes the impacts of two solar eclipses on an isolated microgrid in the municipality of Gracias a Dios, Honduras. The results show the effect on the balance of thermal component utilization within the microgrid and the consequent increase in costs for the community.

articleTitle: Control predictivo robusto basado en modos deslizantes para sistema de generación de energía
abstract: La inserción de los dispositivos de almacenamiento en los sistemas de generación renovable esta tomando cada vez más terreno. En este contexto, el diseño de controladores robustos, que optimicen su desempeño, es fundamental para incrementar la eficiencia y garantizar un funcionamiento seguro y confiable del sistema híbrido frente a la naturaleza intermitente y variable del recurso renovable. Es así que, en este trabajo, se presenta una estrategia de control avanzada para un sistema de generación de energía híbrida con múltiples dispositivos de almacenamiento. La topología de control propuesta combina un Control Predictivo de Matriz Dinámica Cuadrática (QDMC) con técnicas de Modos Deslizantes de Segundo Orden (MDSO). Al integrar las capacidades predictivas con manejo de restricciones y bajo costo computacional del QDMC con la robustez del control por MDSO, este método híbrido permite lograr una mejora significativa en el seguimiento de los objetivos de control, optimizando la convergencia hacia la superficie de deslizamiento respecto al control por modos deslizantes convencional. Los resultados de simulación presentados demuestran el potencial de este enfoque propuesto en la gestión de sistemas de generación de energía híbrida.

articleTitle: Visible Light Communication and Leaky Feeder for 5G and 6G
abstract: This work presents Visible Light Communication (VLC) and Leaky Feeder technologies, explaining their channel models and how they can contribute to current wireless communications. Their main standards are described, and a brief comparison is made between them, highlighting that they can be used either as alternatives or in a complementary way in enclosed spaces, like tunnels, where Wi-Fi may not be efficient. Although these technologies are not new, their implementation is still developing, especially VLC, which has recently gained significant momentum. Finally, due to their characteristics, both VLC and Leaky Feeder can make a valuable contribution to 5G networks and the future development of 6G.

articleTitle: Lighting Control in Combined Direct Solar Lighting Systems with Optical Fiber and Artificial Lighting with LED

authors.preferredName: Carlos Henriques Ventura Do Rosário Oliveira

abstract: The energy crisis and the search for clean energy have led to the development of efficient solutions in various fields. One of the solutions being studied and implemented is direct lighting systems using concentrated sunlight through plastic optical fibers (POF). This work addresses a solution for luminaires, which integrates the optical fiber solution with the well-established LED lighting systems. The purpose of this hybrid solution is to control the illumination level in the environment, compensating for the variation in solar lighting that occurs due to changing atmospheric conditions. Laboratory tests in lighting technology were conducted to verify the solution. The results indicate that it is a good, low-cost solution for solar lighting systems with optical fibers.

articleTitle: Development of an interactive tool for the visualization and training of muscular synergies
abstract: Muscle coordination patterns are crucial for movement control. Events like strokes can disrupt these patterns. This disruption has been correlated with movement dexterity, which implies that the recruitment of muscle coordination patterns may be an effective target for rehabilitation therapies to restore dexterous movement. In this project, a specific tool was developed to evaluate this potential therapeutic effect. Specifically, a human-computer interface was developed, in which a subject’s muscle activity, obtained through surface electromyography, controls a two-dimensional cursor on a screen but only if said activity includes the recruitment of specific muscle coordination patterns. Through visualization of the cursor’s movement on the screen, the tool allows for the subject to receive real-time feedback about their muscle coordination patterns, establishing a “human-in-the-loop” feedback control system. The developed system consists of four interconnected modules through standard communication protocols. Surface electromyography signals are obtained using sensors from Delsys, Inc., which deliver data through eight channels at $\mathbf{2 k H z}$. These samples are collected by a module responsible for serving them to an upstream processing module. This second module is responsible for detecting muscle activation through envelope detection and determination of cursor displacement through a movement speed controller. Finally, two application modules were designed. The first one utilizes the processed data to generate a two-dimensional game with clear objectives for the user and the second one displays a real-time history of muscle activations providing information about the patient’s performance. Future work will validate the usage of this tool for rehabilitation purposes.

articleTitle: Analysis of the Operating History of Brazilian Power Generation Plants using Maintenance Indicators
abstract: Large power generation plants play a crucial role in meeting consumer demand and maintaining the stability of the electrical system. Different types of plants, each with their own operational characteristics, contribute to the complementarity of the electric power system. This study aims to analyze the operational history of six Brazilian plants using data provided by the National System Operator (ONS). Indicators such as Mean Time to Repair (MTTR), Mean Time to Failure (MTTF), Mean Time Between Failures (MTBF), Failure Rate, Total Downtime, and Availability will be calculated. From this analysis, it will be possible to identify which plants have the best indicators and which ones need improvements in their operation and maintenance processes. This type of study is essential to ensure the efficiency and reliability of the Brazilian electrical system, enabling the implementation of more effective preventive and corrective maintenance strategies. The main contribution of this study is to provide a better understanding of the maintenance needs of power generation plants in Brazil, enabling the formulation of policies and practices that ensure the robustness of the national electrical system.

articleTitle: Towards an experience in AI-driven development for programming applied to multimedia using Tabnine
abstract: The development of enjoyable, interesting and meaningful learning experiences in different domains, such as, for example, learning programming languages driven with artificial intelligence (AI) is a current challenge that should be monitored from a longitudinal scope to evidence its true potential. The objective of this work is to contribute to the existing literature on an experience in AI-driven development for programming applied to multimedia, using Tabnine as a central tool. An empirical-analytical research methodology of quantitative, quasi-experimental and longitudinal design is developed. Students who have taken the subject of Programming Applied to Multimedia, from May 2023 to September 2024, of the Multimedia Design career in a Polytechnic University in the city of Guayaquil in Ecuador, participate in the study. The results highlight positive learning factors such as minimizing algorithmic writing time and choice of code, as well as maximizing productivity in the search for a solution, improvements in study commitment, and satisfaction at the time of learning. 91% of the students evidenced their interest and satisfaction in these learning experiences developed by the teachers for learning programming. Future work is focused on longitudinal studies to provide new effective experiences with the use of AI tools that influence academic performance and student ethics.

articleTitle: Real-Time Detection of UAV Small Target’s Infrared Imaging via OSTD-YOLOv8
abstract: Unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) have boosted modern living. Tiny, frail high-density targets, low resolution, complicated backgrounds, noise, and poor real-time exposure performance have augmented due to UAV firms. Realtime recognition in high-altitude (HA) infrared thermal images is intricate. Our fresh OSTD-YOLOv8 is a multi-class target recognition tactic to tackle these issues and spot and classify objects on the HIT-UAV dataset. YOLOv8 is an effective advanced object detection model. Our OSTD-YOLOv8 model detects small objects in HA thermal images with ${90 \%}$ precision, ${91.5 \%}$ recall, ${90.5 \%}$ F1-score, ${89.1 \%}$ AP, and 98% mAP. Our unique approach delivers effective object recognition in difficult thermal imaging conditions. Consequently, this distinctive UAV-focused HA, thermal, target detection scheme can be used.

articleTitle: Control of a Telescope Mount for Astronomical Observations and LEO Satellite Tracking
abstract: This paper presents the development and simulation of a 2-DOF spherical telescope for astronomical observations and LEO satellite tracking, modeled using the EulerLagrange methodology. An adaptive PID controller, optimized with genetic algorithms, ensures robust control. The simulations demonstrate that the telescope’s response converges asymptotically without control input chattering, effectively handling the dynamics of the system.

articleTitle: Thermal Stability of Acrylic Collecting Surface for Acoustic Hail Sensor
abstract: The energy discharged by hailstorms poses a significant threat to human property, ranging from agriculture to vehicles. To prevent damages, a deeper understanding of this phenomenon is essential. Acousto-electric sensors represent a promising option for in-situ measurement of ongoing storms. These sensors utilize piezoelectric elements to acquire electrical signals generated by the vibration of a collecting surface upon impact. The signals are then processed to estimate the energy of the impacts. Given that the collecting surface is exposed to weather conditions, it is important to investigate whether the electrical signals are temperature-dependent. This study presents an evaluation of the thermal stability of the signals obtained from such sensors, using acrylic as the collecting surface. An experiment was designed to simulate hail impacts in a highly repetitive manner, ensuring that temperature is the only variable parameter. The temperature range considered corresponds to the most common ground temperatures during hail events. The results demonstrate excellent stability in both the signals and energy estimations.

articleTitle: Discrete Wavelet Transform for Islanding Detection of Photovoltaic Distributed Generators
abstract: The electric power system is changing, and units that previously only consumed power have begun to inject it into the grid. Photovoltaic generation has grown in recent years and is currently the most widely used source of distributed generation in Brazil. One of the main concerns when connecting a distributed generator (DG) to the grid is unintentional islanding, which occurs when a portion of the grid containing DG and loads remains electrified, but electrically isolated from the rest of the grid. In this case, the DG power supply is not supervised by the grid and can lead to many problems, concerning security and operation. This work proposes a methodology that uses Discrete Wavelet Transform (DWT) for islanding detection, analyzing the voltage signal at the point of common coupling between the utility, DG and loads. A real scenario was used to develop and test the proposed method. For the studied case, the algorithm responded correctly in 100 % of the practical cases evaluated, with detection time between 0.06 s and 0.2 s.

articleTitle: Patch Antenna Design on Transparent Substrate with Circular Polarisation for CubeSat Communications
abstract: The increasing popularity of small satellites, known as CubeSats, has driven the development and adaptation of technologies for these new platforms. This work presents a CubeSat antenna design that can be manufactured using resources available at university. Specifically, the article details the design of a microstrip patch antenna on a transparent polystyrene substrate, with circular polarisation and operating frequency of 5.8 GHz (C-band), paying particular attention to antenna’s integration on-board the CubeSat platform.

articleTitle: Technological Phases of ABDOPRE: a System for Non-Invasive Reduction of Abdominal Hypertension Using Servo-Controlled External Negative Pressure
abstract: Interest in Intra-Abdominal Hypertension (IAH) treatment has increased since the early 2000s at a time the World Society of the Abdominal Compartment Syndrome (WSACS) was founded. The WSACS publishes consensus definitions and clinical practice guidelines for IAH treatament. ABDOPRE is a prototype to reduce intra-abdominal pressure in critically ill patients, applying servo-controlled vacuum. It was originally designed in 2007 to fulfill a clinical need expressed by clinicians at the University Hospital in Uruguay. The goal was to obtain a non-invasive treatment for intra-abdominal hypertension, i.e. when it is higher than 12 mm Hg but still below 20 mm Hg. To achieve its purpose, ABDOPRE uses a vacuum diaphragm pump to reduce the pressure in a bell applied onto the abdomen of the patient. ABDOPRE also monitors the intra-abdominal pressure (IAP) using a bladder catheter, which is a minimally invasive technique. This pressure is used to control the vacuum to apply the treatment protocol defined by the physician. Above 20 mmHg, IAH is refractory to vacuum management and must be solved by surgical decompression. However for IAP below 20 mmHg, clinical management can prevent the pressure from reaching critical levels, potentially avoiding the need for invasive methods. Successive versions of ABDOPRE were developed in 2016, 2020 and 2022. Motivated by the confirmed clinical interest and the conformation of an interdisciplinary team which includes physicians, industrial designers and engineers, ABDOPRE is getting ready in 2024 to contribute to clinical research on intra-abdominal hypertension treatment. ABDOPRE 2024 uses a Raspberry Pi 4 model B with 8GB RAM programmed in Python, as a bedside device with monitoring and treatment functionalities. ABDOPRE includes a WiFi connected desktop application to generate clinical reports as the pressure is monitored at the bedside. ABDOPRE 2024 aims at fulfilling the need of a bedside device needed for clinical monitoring and abdomen pressure depressor therapy.

articleTitle: Overvoltages in a 400 kV Transmission Line with Y-shaped Composite Pylon: Impact of Line Parameter Calculation Formulations
abstract: This paper assesses the impact of employing two distinct formulations, derived from different definitions for the overhead conductor voltages, in calculating transmission line parameters for assessing lightning-induced overvoltages in overhead lines installed on a composite material transmission tower featuring a $\mathbf{Y}$-shaped composite pylon. One of the formulations uses Pettersson’s equations, which are based on the definition of voltage on conductors, providing a physically more consistent approach. While the other formulation uses Carson’s equations, which are based on the definition of potential on conductors, offering a physically less consistent approach, this latter formulation is typically used in EMT-type programs. The results reveal significant differences between the physically more consistent formulation and those typically employed in EMT-type programs when comparing lightning-induced overvoltages in overhead lines installed on a Y-shaped pylon. These differences become more pronounced with increasing soil resistivity and may be crucial in determining occurrences of backflashover on the line.

articleTitle: URUCON 2024 Abstract Page
Predictive Modeling for Patient Hospitalization: Enhancing Healthcare Outcomes
abstract: The main motivator for this project is to make improvements to the healthcare system and resource management so that it is easier for hospitals and emergency responders to transport patients based on need and to allow emergency room patients to be treated based on need as well. This information will allow municipalities nationwide to reassess their hospital and related care capacities to better suit trends in their regions. Binary classification was utilized to achieve this, employing various models and concluding with an ensemble classifier that uses KNN, RF, AB, GNB, and XGB as the initial estimators, and GB as the final estimator. The accuracy hovers around 0.96, AUC around 0.90, precision macro average around.95, recall macro average around 0.91, and f1-score macro average around $\mathbf{0.93}$.

articleTitle: Adaptive and Hierarchical Voltage Control: The Overview of Real Time Methodology for Voltage Regulators
abstract: This paper introduces an innovative method for adaptive and hierarchical voltage control (AHVC) in distribution power systems. The proposed method is a hybrid approach that integrates a centralized control module with distributed modules. The centralized module, referred to as the Hierarchical Control (HC), works in conjunction with the supervisory control and data acquisition system (SCADA). The distributed module, known as the Local Control (LC), is connected to each Step Voltage Regulator (VR). This control system operates with individual settings and in real-time, providing a robust solution for application in distribution lines. It enhances voltage control flexibility for various scenarios, including varying or seasonal loads, reconfiguration switching, and contingencies (self-healing). The detailed analysis of each step in the method allows for the evaluation of its benefits and integration with supervision and control tools. Additionally, it facilitates local processing to define equipment settings, leading to a distributed intelligence system that further leverages the potential of smart grids.

articleTitle: Techno-Economic Assesment of a Distributed Generation System for Biogas from Wastewater Treatment Plants
abstract: In this study, we aim to conduct a comprehensive techno-economic analysis of a distributed generation system using biogas produced from a wastewater treatment plant. Our methodology involves a case study of an anaerobic wastewater treatment plant in Cochabamba, Bolivia. Initially, we estimate the theoretical biogas flow production and propose a general method for this estimation. Subsequently, we design the storage and treatment systems for the biogas. Following this, we design the distributed generation system in accordance with local regulations. Finally, we perform an economic assessment considering the hours of electrical energy injected into the National Interconnected System (NIS) versus the self-supply hours throughout the day. Additionally, we account for the variable cost of energy in Bolivia based on the time of day, conducting an economic comparison accordingly. The results indicate an average biogas production of $7859.07 \mathrm{Nm} 3 /$ day, with a reference output of 300 kW yielding the highest savings and annual benefits concluding that biogas produced through anaerobic wastewater treatment is a viable non-seasonal and renewable energy source.

articleTitle: Assessing Bias in Citizen Science Data through Linear Regression
abstract: Citizen Science Data is a valuable resource for addressing ecological questions. Some initiatives like eBird have gained prominence since its establishment in 2002. This platform has emerged as a vital source for collecting birdwatching data, particularly beneficial for ornithology and ecology. However, the semi-structured nature of this data introduces potential biases during the collection process. In ecology, bias—especially in the context of citizen or community science—refers to a systematic error that can distort data collection and analysis, potentially leading to inaccurate conclusions about ecological relationships. These ecological biases include taxonomic, spatial, and temporal factors. While established preprocessing techniques can mitigate some of these issues, specific covariates necessitate more refined treatments to ensure the reliability of the conclusions drawn from this data. This study introduces a Linear Regression-based hypothesis testing technique from correlation measures to evaluate bias in Citizen Science Data corresponding to sightings of the Monk Parakeet (Myiopsitta monachus). The results demonstrate that this straightforward yet potent model can capture sufficient variance to eliminate effort variables and preserve other covariates for future research. The proposed approach leverages the observed significance and the coefficient of determination to assess performance.

articleTitle: URUCON 2024 Abstract Page
Design of multipurpose terrestrial robotic platform
abstract: This article presents the project and development of an accessible robotic platform designed for general purposes, especially for academic use, to support research and development in the field of terrestrial robots, including autonomous, teleoperated or radio-controlled robots. The platform primarily consists of a modular aluminum chassis, a pair of tracks driven by DC motors with planetary gearboxes, an electronic system comprising motor power drivers, and sensors such as IMU, GPS, and LiDAR. The system is integrated with the ROS framework using a Raspberry Pi4. A 3D CAD design was created, and the noncommercial mechanical components were 3D printed. The robotic platform was then assembled and tested. Based on the locomotion tests performed in radio-controlled mode on both paved and off-road terrains, the speed, agility, and obstacle traversal capability were evaluated and found to be satisfactory as planned in the project. Additionally, the 3D CAD model of the platform was exported to RVIZ and GAZEBO simulation environments, making it a simple and accessible tool for various research and development applications.

articleTitle: Design optimization for large-scale solar photovoltaic power plants in Uruguay
abstract: This article focuses on maximizing the relative net present value of a photovoltaic power plant by applying optimization techniques to its design. The case study refers to a 50 MW (AC) plant with parameters specific to the north-western region of Uruguay. Test scenarios are created by exploring variations in energy prices, contract duration, DC cable costs, project discount rate, among others. The control variables include the tilt of the photovoltaic panels, the number of series and parallel connections, the number of rows and columns of photovoltaic blocks in the sub-park, the distance between the rows, and the ratio of the DC power of the photovoltaic panels to the nominal AC power of the plant. According to the experimental results, the optimized relative net present value ranges from 1.37 to 1.39, with optimized capacity factors around 24%.

articleTitle: MOP: first industrial application of Stochastic Dual Dynamic Programming for optimization of the Uruguayan power system
abstract: This paper introduces MOP, a development that implements the first application of Stochastic Dual Dynamic Programming (SDDP) for optimization of the Uruguayan power system. The study addresses the challenge of efficiently managing a system characterized by a large hydroelectric component and an increasing integration of non conventional renewable energy sources.A detailed case study of the Uruguayan system is conducted to demonstrate the effectiveness of the SDDP algorithm. The analysis highlights robust convergence and compares the performance of SDDP with standard Stochastic Dynamic Programming methods (SDP). The results show that the SDDP algorithm effectively manages system complexity and yields accurate optimization outcomes. Additionally, the successful application in the current system suggests the scalability of the method to systems with more state variables.

articleTitle: A low-cost open-access navigation system for UAV applications as a redundancy system
abstract: Inertial navigation systems (INS) based on micro-electromechanical sensors (MEMS) assisted by global positioning systems (GPS) are widely used for aerospace navigation applications and provide data with high accuracy. However, they are costly and fragile. This work addresses the development of a low-cost and open-source GPS-assisted INS for navigation applications where the accuracy, practicality, and replicability obtained in this module are attractive for redundant systems in UAVs, even in tasks with risk of loss or damage. The experimental tests show the records obtained during the flight performance of the Phantom 4 Pro drone in which data from the low-cost INS is compared with the primary vehicle system.

articleTitle: Locomotion of Rolling Microrobots Under Rotating Magnetic Fields Within Fluid Media
abstract: Medicine advances more and more with the development of new technologies. One is microrobotics, which could be used for drug delivery, endoscopy, and others. This work shows the locomotion of magnetic spinning/rolling microrobots with different geometries (sphere, cube, and cylinder) according to different scenarios: displacement in different widths channels and in slope. Furthermore, the three microrobots are tested in a more complex scenario, where a proportional closed-loop control controls their positions in a curved channel with bifurcations and obstacles to simulate a human artery.

articleTitle: Generation of High-Voltage Oscillating Impulse Waveforms
abstract: Conventional tests for HV equipment include lightning and switching impulse test, both having unidirectional waveforms. However, transients in high-voltage networks, generated by switching operations, have also oscillating waveforms different of those produced by lightning storms, which are of exponential type. Most impulse generators are designed for the latter, so it is necessary to modify their configurations to achieve an oscillating behavior. This paper presents a design method for that modification, adding an oscillation to the initial time of the exponential waveform. The proposed modifications were implemented on an impulse generator and tested in a HV laboratory.

articleTitle: Accurate estimation of solar PV power plant capacity factors in Uruguay through detailed quality control and satellite gap filling
abstract: This study implements a methodology to produce accurate, gap-free time series of solar irradiance and PV generation data for a large photovoltaic (PV) power plant in Uruguay. Addressing the challenge of data gaps in solar energy monitoring, the work employs quality control techniques, satellite-based solar irradiance estimation, solar radiation and PV models, and gap-filling procedures to generate a comprehensive five-year dataset at 10-minute intervals. The resulting dataset allows detailed analysis of solar resource availability, PV production and capacity factors. The study finds an average capacity factor of 22.4% over the fiveyear period, with monthly variations ranging from 14.1% to 28.1%. This work provides the first precise assessment of PV plant capacity factors in Uruguay, providing valuable insights for grid management and future solar energy investments.

articleTitle: Management of the Electrical and Thermal Demand of a Social Housing in Argentina
abstract: Procrear is a social housing program in Argentina that has delivered tens of thousands of homes to families across the country. In the province of Córdoba, the thermal conditioning requirement for these houses is elevated, due to the weather, and consequently the consume for energy as well. In this article the thermal behavior of a reference house of this program (Pampeana Norte I) is analyzed through an equivalent resistive-capacitive dynamic model. Additionally, a strategy to optimize thermal and electrical management under a time-of-use pricing scheme is proposed. The optimization strategy, based on a genetic algorithm, and the developed RC model, aims to improve human thermal comfort and minimize electricity costs. The optimization determines the temperature limits of air conditioning units and includes the management of the start time of three devices which are time-shiftable. Finally, this strategy is compared to another non-optimized control strategy, improving the average thermal comfort in a 39% and reducing the electrical cost near of 16%. In conclusion, the dynamic simulations show that the trade-off between thermal comfort and electricity costs can result in a win-win strategy by optimizing the air-conditioning unit usage.

articleTitle: Strategies for Acquiring Dosimetry of a Non-Autonomous UV-C Light Disinfection Robot at 254 nm
abstract: Antimicrobial resistance is a significant global concern that could result in millions of annual deaths by 2050. While vaccines serve as preventive methods, there is a need for decontamination of already contaminated environments. In hospitals, traditional decontamination involves manual cleaning and chemical disinfection, which are labor-intensive, prone to errors, and can be harmful to humans. As an alternative, UVC light has been used as a faster and more effective disinfection method, as it damages the DNA/RNA of microorganisms, preventing their replication. UV-C disinfection robots have been increasingly adopted, though precise information on dosimetry and optimal positioning is still lacking. The aim of this study is to assess the reach and effectiveness of a non-autonomous UV-C robot operating at 254 nm with a power of 3900 W. UV irradiation doses, UV-VIS spectrum, and a model for irradiance fields were determined based on experimental data to ascertain the UV doses delivered by the system to the target surface or airborne microbes. Dosimetric films sensitive to UV-C energy, commercially available, were employed to evaluate radiation doses in different spatial regions, with their accuracy compared to UV spectroradiometry techniques. Both dosimetric films and spectroradiometer results indicate rapid and effective action of the equipment over an unshaded area of $\mathbf{1 2. 2 5}$ square meters, with greater UV intensity variation closer to the source.

articleTitle: Optimal Sizing of Battery Energy Storage Systems in Grid-Connected Power Systems
abstract: This paper presents a novel methodology for optimal sizing of multiple Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS) in grid-connected Hybrid Generation Systems (HGS), focusing on centralized dispatch of wind and photovoltaic sources. Using Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO), the study evaluates key reliability indicators, such as dispatch expectations, curtailment reduction, and grid impact, to determine the optimal BESS size. Climatological data from Brazil and load profiles from the Brazilian Northeast system are utilized to assess the BESS impact on the grid. Applied to two configurations on the IEEE 14-bus test grid, the methodology identifies optimal BESS capacities of ${3 3 . 3 3}$ MWh for Site A and 19.47 MWh for Site B, achieving reductions of $8.15 \%$ in system inflexibility, ${9 . 0 9 \%}$ in curtailment potential, and ${8 . 3 4 \%}$ in slack-bus import fluctuations.

articleTitle: Análisis crítico de los captores activos ESE y propuesta de método para determinar la velocidad de un trazador ascendente durante el ensayo dedicado
abstract: Se llevó a cabo un análisis crítico por el cual un captor de descargas atmosféricas (pararrayos) puede ser catalogado como activo tipo ESE (Early Streamer Emission). Este tipo de captores activos utilizan como una de las principales variables a la velocidad del trazador ascendente, y en conjunto con otras obtenidas a partir del ensayo dedicado se desprende un radio de protección extra en comparación a un captor convencional. Se hace relevante la capacidad de determinar la velocidad del trazador ascendente durante el ensayo dedicado. Se implementó un método utilizando fibras ópticas para captar la luz emitida por la ruptura de la rigidez dieléctrica del aire. Se probó el método propuesto y se demostró que puede ser utilizado para determinar la velocidad del trazador ascendente previo a la descarga en ensayo de los captores activos ESE.

articleTitle: Energy production related to bifacial photovoltaic power plants in the scope of the ground albedo impact
abstract: The objective of this work is to analyze the impact of ground albedo on energy generation in bifacial photovoltaic plants. The methodology includes computer simulations of energy generation in a bifacial photovoltaic plant using different types of ground looking albedos response, and a case study of bifacial photovoltaic pilot unit in the field of a hydroelectric power plant is considered. Following the simulations, a financial viability is developed in view of some type of albedo soils, using a levelised cost of energy-based analysis. The results of this analysis indicated that some types of soils have a lower LCOE compared to others, supporting the hypothesis that bifacial technology enables gains in both energy generation performance and financial viability.

articleTitle: Robust Blind Linear Unmixing for Correlated Multimodal Images in Medical Applications
abstract: In this work, we introduce a new algorithm for robust blind linear unmixing focused in correlated multimodal images (CMI) with emphasis on medical applications. Our proposal is based on a linear model between end-members and abundances, and additive Gaussian and sparse noise components. The end-members represent spectral, time or morphological information, and their abundances denote their spatial contributions in the CMIs. Our formulation for blind linear umixing presents an iterative optimization scheme that uses a convex cost function, and jointly estimates end-members and their abundances, and a sparse noise component. The iterative methodology relies on cyclic coordinate descent optimization, constrained quadratic estimation and L1-regularization. In our evaluation, we consider synthetic datasets of biological tissue absorbance by hyperspectral imaging, and multi-spectral fluorescence life-time imaging. Our proposal was compared with five algorithms from the literature in linear unmixing, and it was able to provide the best compromise between estimation performance and complexity.

articleTitle: A workaround to indirectly estimate the distribution of classes for an Autonomous System
abstract: Prefix-classes group network prefixes that are equivalent with respect to the choice of the next-hop border gateway within an Autonomous System (AS). Clustering the routing information is such way significantly reduces the volume of data needed to analyze or design a network, from several million incoming updates to a few hundred classes, while still finding optimal routes. Existing methods for calculating prefix classes rely upon detailed internal data of the AS under study, which is rarely available. This research proposes a new stochastic method to estimate prefix classes for any AS using only publicly available information. This probabilistic model was tested on a real network and achieved a high degree of accuracy.
